check.heap_table.caveat.staging: Staging tables that are bulk-loaded and truncated can be fine as heaps.
check.heap_table.fix: Add a clustered index, usually on the primary key or an ever-increasing column such as an identity or creation time. Plan it as a maintenance operation: it rewrites the table.
check.heap_table.info.description: Heaps grow forwarded records and can't be read in key order; most OLTP tables should be clustered.
check.heap_table.info.title: Large tables without a clustered index
check.heap_table.summary.forwarded: Reads have followed a forwarding pointer to another page {count} times {since}: each one is an extra random read.
check.heap_table.summary.forwarded_per_d: Reads have followed a forwarding pointer to another page {count} times {since} (about {per_day} a day): each one is an extra random read.
check.heap_table.summary.heap: {table} is stored as a heap. Updates that grow a row leave forwarding pointers behind, deleted space isn't reclaimed well, and every nonclustered index lookup has to go through a row identifier.
check.heap_table.summary.no_primary_key: It has no primary key either.
check.heap_table.summary.primary_key: It does have a primary key, just not a clustered one.
